Power grid reliability issues then become a constant worry, as these breakdowns can cascade throughout the system, triggering power outages that leave entire communities in the dark. This lack of power grid maintenance is a ticking time bomb, increasing the risk of not just localized blackouts, but potentially even a power grid collapse, a scenario that would have catastrophic consequences. Frequent power outages are another problem that goes along with an old power grid. The frequency with which power grid blackouts are increasing isn’t just an inconvenience; it’s a symptom of a deeper illness. Imagine the doctor performing a critical surgery plunged into darkness, the CEO losing crucial data during a presentation due to a sudden power surge, or entire production lines grinding to a halt in factories. The impact of power outages on the economy and human flourishing can be devastating, with businesses losing revenue, productivity plummeting and human lives being endangered. The vulnerabilities of the aging power grid extend beyond physical breakdowns. Power grid security is a growing concern as the system becomes increasingly reliant on digital control systems, which can be compromised by both cyber and electromagnetic pulse attacks. Malicious actors, both foreign and domestic, are constantly seeking new ways to exploit these weaknesses. The effects of power grid cyberattacks would cripple entire regions, plunging millions into darkness and causing widespread chaos. These dire consequences highlight the urgent need to bolster our cyber defenses and build a more secure power grid. When it comes to the power grid, the threats aren’t all man-made… Climate change and the power grid are intricately linked. Extreme weather power outages have become more frequent due  climate change and can cause major damage to our power infrastructure.

A terrorist attack on the power system would lack the dramatic impact of the attacks in New York, Madrid, or London. It would not immediately kill many people or make for spectacular television footage of bloody destruction. But if it were carried out in a carefully planned way, by people who knew what they were doing, it could deny large regions of the country access to bulk system power for weeks or even months. An event of this magnitude and duration could lead to turmoil, widespread public fear, and an image of helplessness that would play directly into the hands of the terrorists. If such
